progress.stage: resolver + both doors + every naming surface verified over the real index and the real server; the constructor case still needs V1's fresh-install frame showing the label, so the issue is NOT closable yet
fixes: src/lsp/identity.ts (new, the ONE owner): the member-resolution rules moved out of the impact door, where the graph door had re-implemented its own call. Both doors read this module now (impact.ts delegates, graph_request.ts imports the resolver + the record builder), so a rule change cannot land on one surface only.

src/lsp/graph_request.ts: a member target the engine whitelist excludes no longer travels as an unlabeled root — the substitution rides the payload as a declared `resolution` record (memberName/ownerName/through), and a hinted request whose root lands outside the hint is refused instead of silently relabeled.

src/lsp/graph_request.ts (declared-error half): a genuinely absent symbol used to escape as the engine's bare "Symbol '<name>' not found", contradicting GRAPH-TRANSPORT.md's own prefix contract (clients match `bb/graph:` to tell a declared error from a bug). It is wrapped into a declared `bb/graph:` reason; any OTHER engine failure is still thrown untouched, because prefixing a real bug would mislabel it as expected behaviour. The doc row was corrected to match the code.

ide/vscode/src/identity-label.ts (new): the panel-title rule was extracted out of graph-panel.ts (which imports `vscode`) into a vscode-free module, because a rule that cannot run in a gate cannot be verified — and this one had silently failed the owner (a constructor graph opening titled `Store` with nothing said). graph-panel re-exports it, so hub/impact/graph all render through ONE rule.

script/m55/t1-fixture.ts + script/m55/verify-identity.ts (new): the fixture (member target, a SECOND constructor for the ambiguity case, an accessor, an absent name, a direct root) and the suite over the REAL indexer, the REAL server and the REAL renderer — 38 checks, 5 mutants.
findings: a TypeScript getter is stored as `property`, which is outside the traversal whitelist — so an accessor is a member target too and is now labeled rather than silently relabeled (asserted from the stored type, not assumed)
the accessor invariant is derived at run time from the stored symbol_type, so the gate cannot pass vacuously if a future analyzer starts storing getters as traversable methods
remaining: V1's fresh-install frame reproducing the constructor case with the label visible (closure requirement)
T3 owns the "which edges are usages" half; T1 only owns identity

evidence.scope: resolver rules over the real index + boundary rules over a real sqlite seed + both doors over the real dist server + the title/label and render surfaces, with 5 planted defects

progress.stage: component + wire legs verified; the in-editor Call-hierarchy leg is still pending V1's rig (closure requirement), so the issue is NOT closable yet
fixes: src/lsp/positions.ts (M24.P1 owner): a stored byte 0 could not convert (`byte < 1` -> null), so prepareCallHierarchy returned a declared absence for the FIRST symbol of any file whose declaration starts at offset 0 — the live demo's `deep`/`loop`/`Store` were unreachable in call hierarchy. Byte 0 is unambiguous (per-line columns are 1-based), so it now converts to line 1 column 1; a byte 0 on any other line stays declared-unconvertible. Gated by 8 row cases + 3 new mutants in script/m24/verify-positions.ts (P1 21/21, 11/11).

src/lsp/call_hierarchy.ts: receiver classification read `this.items.get(...)` as `this.` (recursion) because the receiver ended with a separator — the analyzer's name-resolution artifact was therefore kept and the member listed itself as its own caller. Classification now uses the receiver's LAST segment plus the symbol's own names (qualified_name owner), and the receiver text is reported without the trailing separator.

src/lsp/call_hierarchy.ts: incoming/outgoing rendered the engine's deeper hops (depth > 0) as callers/callees with an approximate position (`top` listed as a caller of `deep` through `mid`; a mutual pair listed each function as its own caller). LSP's lists are DIRECT relations, so a stored `calls` row from an indexed caller whose own source never invokes the name is now DROPPED and declared in droppedEdges.

script/m24/lsp_harness.ts (M24.V1): four L2 hover legs still asserted the pre-wire-law shape (flat `data.name`, top-level `provenance`, `{contents:null}` absence) and sat KNOWN-GAP while the server was correct; they now assert the declared contract (data.symbol.*, data.provenance.source, wire null) and the L5 leg asserts the reported call site slices back to the invoked name.
remaining: in-editor leg: hover -> Call hierarchy in a pinned editor, the callers rendered, clicking one landing on the CALL SITE with the correct symbol (frame + machine assertion) — V1's rig
defectsReportedToOtherLanes: a file-absolute symbol row whose offset also fits the target line's byte length is still read as a per-line column by resolveRowByteColumns (pre-existing declared ambiguity, now recorded in P1.json's limitations); removing it needs a writer-side convention flag from the indexer lane
